summary.prose: The build changes the call-sequence label first, then writes the page script that finds code references and posts a click, then adds the pane's rule for taking such a click from its own companion frame, then puts the script into the three page shells, and last pins the script's reference grammar to the chat page's. The pane rule and the page script are built and tested on their own, so the feature only works end to end once both are in; the host's check of the file is not touched. Pages already written are not changed.

tasks.title: Label a call frame with its repo-relative path and line
tasks.summary: Give frameLabel and buildCallSequenceIR an optional repoRoot. With a root, a frame's label reads 'name (path:line)' where path is the file relative to the root with forward slashes; without a root, or for a file outside it, the label keeps the base-name form. Pass scope.repoRoot from makeExtract, the builder's only production caller. Node ids, edge ids and citations are not touched.
acceptanceChecks: A frame inside the root is labelled 'name (relative/path.ts:line)' with forward slashes on every platform
A frame outside the root, or a build with no root, keeps the 'name (base.ts:line)' label
Node ids, edge ids and citations are unchanged, and the existing three-argument callers of the builder still compile and pass

tasks.title: Write the code-reference page script
tasks.summary: Create src/docgen/render/code-ref-script.ts, which imports from neither page shell and exports CODE_REF_SCRIPT. The script marks each element whose own text holds a code reference (a path with a directory part, an optional :N, :N-M or :N:C), records the marked element and position at pointerdown in a capture-phase listener, and on a click that moved at most 4 pixels posts { type: 'insrc-open-code-ref', path, line? } to the parent. It marks elements without splitting text nodes, stops no event, leaves pointer capture alone, and runs once on load and again when asked after a diagram is drawn.
acceptanceChecks: An element whose text holds a path and line is marked and a click posts that path and line; a path with no line posts the path alone
Text with no reference, and a bare file name, are not marked and post nothing
Marking changes no text node, and the script stops no event and does not touch pointer capture
A click on a marked box inside a viewport that captures the pointer posts the reference, and a press, a move past 4 pixels and a release posts nothing

tasks.title: Add the pane's rule for a reference posted by its companion frame
tasks.summary: In vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-panel.ts, add rvFrameMessage and register it as a window message handler: it acts only when the message's source is the current companion frame's contentWindow, the type is 'insrc-open-code-ref', the path is a non-empty string of bounded length and the line, when present, is a positive integer. It then posts the existing open-code-ref payload to the host. The frame keeps sandbox allow-scripts only; the host's check is untouched. The pane rule stands on its own: it is exercised by posting the frame message straight to the window handler, not through a page.
acceptanceChecks: A test that posts the frame message directly to the pane's window handler, from the companion frame's window, with a valid path and line sees the same path and line posted to the host as an open-code-ref message
A message from any other window, or with a missing, non-string or oversized path, or a line that is not a positive integer, is ignored
The frame is still created with sandbox 'allow-scripts' only, and the existing docs-companion, docs-content and decision messages are handled as before

tasks.title: Carry the script in the three page shells
tasks.summary: Import CODE_REF_SCRIPT into the companion page shell (src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts), the docgen Mermaid shell (src/docgen/render/shell.ts) and the docgen subprocess fallback (assembleFallbackShell in src/docgen/render/fallback.ts) and inline it. The two Mermaid shells run the marking after mermaid.run resolves, and a page with no Mermaid visual and the fallback run it once at load. A marked element gets a pointer cursor from the page's own style.
acceptanceChecks: The companion shell, the docgen Mermaid shell and the docgen fallback shell each carry CODE_REF_SCRIPT, imported from the one module, with no import cycle between the shells and the module
In the two Mermaid shells the marking runs after the diagram is drawn; a page with no Mermaid visual and the fallback mark references at load
A marked element is styled as clickable (a pointer cursor) in the companion shell and in both docgen shells
A page built without any reference is otherwise unchanged and still renders its header, narrative, view and description tables

tasks.title: Pin the script's grammar to the chat page's
tasks.summary: Add a contract test that reads the chat page's CREF_EXT and CREF_CORE from vscode-plugin/src/chat/link-markup.ts and checks that the page script's grammar equals them except for the directory group, which the script requires to be non-empty.
acceptanceChecks: The test fails when the page script's extension list or line forms differ from the chat page's
The only allowed difference is the required directory part, and the test says so
